lesson_1.title: Constant Time O(1)

lesson_1.title: Linear Growth O(n)

lesson_1.title: Quadratic Growth O(n²)

lesson_1.title: Dominant Term Analysis

lesson_1.title: Worst-Case Branching

optimizations.title: Optimize: Duplicate Search
task: The pre-loaded `find_duplicates` function is functionally correct, but it relies on an inefficient brute-force approach. Let's fix that.
Refactor the code structure to achieve an O(n) Linear Time complexity.
1. Look at the Complexity tab. The real-time analysis displays an O(n²) bottleneck in Global Time because the nested loops perform redundant comparisons.
2. Delete the inner loop block and its condition. You only need a single loop to solve this problem.
3. Create a variable before the loop (like an empty list) to keep track of elements you have already seen.
4. Inside your single loop, check if the current element is already present in your tracking list. If it is, return that element immediately.
5. If it isn't, append the element to your tracking list and allow the loop to proceed.
6. Keep the final `return -1` outside the loop, and check the analyzer to verify your refactored O(n) algorithm.
